package.name: emissions-and-polution-sources-in-bulgaria
package.author: Ministry for Environment and Water
package.notes:
All entities producing air, water, soil emissions or any other kind of pollution are registered with the Environmental Ministry. The public registry displays information on all of them including yearly reports of the emissions, ways they were measured, location and responsible person/company. The information is contained in HTML pages and is not downloadable.

![emissions dashboard](http://opendata.yurukov.net/ecology/res/img/ecology.png)

In this project I scraped the data, geotaged all locations and put them on an [interactive dashboard](http://opendata.yurukov.net/ecology/). The data will be updated each year. It is interesting to see how regulation helped some factories decrease their emissions with a couple of hundred percent. There are some troubling cases, where independent measurements how increase of fine particle pollution, while the industry report decrease in emissions.

package.name: police-budget-spending
package.author: Interior Ministry of Bulgaria
package.notes:
All budget funded public organizations in Bulgaria are obliged to publish daily reports of fund transfers and payments. These reports should specify general reason for payment (salaries, loan repayments, support, etc.), but don't contain individual sums, beneficiaries or specific reason for payment (e.g. procurement, settlement). Also, there's no defined format, in which these reports should be published. Some provide Excel sheets, some screenshots, but most put PDFs on their pages. 

The following scraping and visualization project focuses on the data of the Interior Ministry. It came into focus after tens of thousands of policemen and -woman were transferred from all over the country to the capital to counter the massive anti-government protests. Questions were raised how were they paid and how much did the unnecessary police pressure cost the budget. 

![Police spending dashboard](http://opendata.yurukov.net/spending/mvr/res/mvrspending.png)

The [dashboard above](http://opendata.yurukov.net/spending/mvr/) allows combing though the data with regard to period, reason and department which issued the payment. Patterns already emerge when it comes to certain payments. For example, there's more than a [160-fold increase](http://opendata.yurukov.net/spending/mvr/#130801,140126&88) in "unspecified" spending with the new cabinet. The filters in the dashboard can be hotlinked though the URL. It was created using D3.js, Crossfilter and DC.js. Source is in [GitHub](https://github.com/yurukov/Police-spending).

The data is scraped **daily** and converted in CSV files with reports for each department. The dataset can be downloaded as a ZIP file.

package.name: res-bulgaria
package.author: Boyan Yurukov | Agency for sustainable development
package.notes:
This is a transformed dataset with all renewable energy sold in Bulgaria in 2012. It also contains data on the power stations, owners, capacity and creation date. The locations of the power stations are geotaged.

Here you can find the visualization of the data:

[http://opendata.yurukov.net/vei/en](http://opendata.yurukov.net/vei/en)

This is the original source:

[http://www.seea.government.bg/index.php...](http://www.seea.government.bg/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=9279&Itemid=234&lang=bg)
package.title: Renewable energy in Bulgaria

package.name: realtime-birth-data-in-bulgaria
package.author: Bulgarian Health Ministry, National Statistics Institute, Boyan Yurukov
package.notes: The public health ministry has released real time data on births in Bulgaria. The data is submited with maximum 3 day delay from each hospital in the country and summarized by reagions. I've scraped it and published it in CSV format. On [home page](http://opendata.yurukov.net/birth/) of the data, you'll find that I've mixed it with the latest census data (Feb 2011) and mashed it up into an interactive map.
package.title: Realtime birth data in Bulgaria

package.name: public-regs-bulgaria
package.author: Access to Information Programme
package.notes: This an [overview](http://www.publicregisters.info/) of all public registries in Bulgaria with details who supports them and if they are up to date, what format is the data, what law dictates the need for the registry. The overview is created by [Access to Information Programme](http://www.aip-bg.org/en/) and for some reason is with all-rights-reserved license.
package.title: Registry of all public registries in Bulgaria

package.name: open-data-of-the-bulgarian-parliament
package.author: Bulgarian Parliament | Remixed - Boyan Yurukov
package.notes:
This data is corrected, indexed and enriched open data from the Bulgarian parliament. Each xml file in this dataset links to individual profiles with the full information for an MP, parliament group, committee, etc. There' s data on the external consultants for each parliament entity, transcripts, individual MP votes, agendas, etc. Each datapoint links to the original information source.

While the parliament releases a lot of open data in XML and CSV form, most of it is not in valid format. Also, a lot of information that can be found on the website is missing. I fixed the data and enriched it. It will be cached and updated twice a week. There are also [RSS](http://feeds.feedburner.com/BGParliament_zakoni) and [twitter](http://twitter.com/#!/narodnosabranie) feeds for law propositions. 

You can find a full index of the data on the [project's page](http://parliament.yurukov.net/index_en.html). There you'll also find XSD that describes the format. You can also get the [source](https://github.com/yurukov/Bulgarian-Parliament-Open-Data) of the scripts used to compile this data.
package.title: Open data of the Bulgarian Parliament

package.name: fallen_bg_soldiers
package.author: Bulgarian Archive Agency
package.notes:
This is a dataset with information on fallen Bulgarian soldiers during the Balkan wars 1912-1913. Hundreds of documents have been digitized by the Bulgarian agency for archives resulting in thousands of records. Each record include the names of the deceased, place of birth and year of joining the army, date, place and reason for the death and place of the grave if known. There are also notes, reference and scanned image of the original document. 

In the dataset you will find all this information and links or reference numbers to the original source and scanned images. I've cleaned up the dates, places and reasons for death making the uniform. I've added comments in the notes field wherever a change was needed.

You'll find photos and documents on the [original website](http://archives.bg/balkanwars/) of the archive and the dataset and (soon) visualizations on the [opendata page](http://opendata.yurukov.net/balkanwars/).
package.title: Fallen Bulgarian soldiers during the Balkan wars 1912-1913

package.name: fairelections-bg2011
package.author: FairRlections.Eu
package.notes: This data was crowd sourced over the course of several months before and during the 2011 Bulgarian presidential and local elections. The description is in Bulgarian, but is easily translatable with Google trans. The website has an [English version](https://www.fairelections.eu/?l=en_US) as well. There are about 320 approved incidents and quite a lot of those are verified though media, police and election committee reports.
package.title: Presidential and local elections in Bulgaria - crowdsoruced data on irregularities and fraud

package.name: eu-projects-bg
package.notes:
This is a [database](http://umispublic.minfin.bg/) with all EU projects, beneficiaries, regions, programs and paid out sums since Bulgaria joined the EU. It has search, regional maps and the capability to export all data in open formats.

There is no single API, but rather a complete tool for filtering and exporting data.

Data has been downloaded and visualized on [opendata.yurukov.net/eu/](http://opendata.yurukov.net/eu/)
package.title: Data on all EU projects in Bulgaria

package.name: energy-production-in-bulgaria
package.author: Boyan Yurukov | ESO
package.notes: The Bulgarian electricity system operator is updating a page with the latest production and system load each 35 seconds. The figures are grouped by plant type. There's no historic data so I'm scraping it. This is the api to access the information. The full dump can be downloaded as a ZIP. It's updated daily at 0:00 GMT.
package.title: Energy production and consumption in Bulgaria

package.name: data-on-missing-person-cases-in-bulgaria
package.author: Boyan Yurukov | Crowd sourcing
package.notes: Open data on solved and unsolved cases of missing people in Bulgaria. This data is gathered though crowd sourcing - from police reports, submissions from relatives and news in the media. The data for the solved cases is striped of any personal information.
package.title: Data on missing person cases in Bulgaria

package.name: bulgaria-vat-firms
package.author: NRA Bulgaria
package.notes:
There's a public registry of firms in Bulgaria registered by the VAT law. It is updated daily and downloadable only if one registers and receives a daily code. No historic record exists.

I've started a script which downloads this list daily, compiles a diff list and statistics on the added, changed and removed companies. It also fixes the encoding. 

All the data is available as separate archives [here](http://opendata.yurukov.net/business/data) and on the [official site](http://opendata.yurukov.net/business/) you'll find visualizations.
package.title: Firms in Bulgaria registered for VAT

package.name: bulgaria-schools
package.author: Bulgarian Ministry of Education and Science
package.notes: The data was collected from the published reports of the Bulgarian Ministry of Education and Science: http://mon.bg/left_menu/budget The geoJSON data on the regions of Bulgaria is extracted from the OpenStreetMap definitions. Visualization of the data can be seen here: http://opendata.yurukov.net/educ/map/
package.title: Data on school kids in Bulgaria

package.name: bulgarian-state-security
package.author: State Security Committee | Boyan Yurukov
package.notes: Public data on former Bulgarian state security operatives derived from reports of a special committee bringing light into the subject. These reports are in PDF form. After scraping the information, I've cleaned the data and released it in a usable form. Nevertheless, individual lines should be checked against the original reports. Full information on the dataset, as well as all the referenced reports can be found on [this website](http://opendata.yurukov.net/statesecurity/).
package.title: Former Bulgarian state security operatives

package.name: bulgarian-municipalities
package.author: Boyan Yurukov
package.notes:
This is a GeoJson of local municipalities in Bulgaria. The properties contain a unique ID, name and province name in Bulgarian. The features are extracted from the world definition of OpenStreetMap. The file can be used directly for generating overlays in maps.

Wiki page on municipalities:
http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Municipalities_of_Bulgaria

Example of how it can be used:
http://opendata.yurukov.net/educ/map/
package.title: GeoJSON of Bulgarian municipalities

package.name: bulgarian-embassies
package.author: Boyan Yurukov
package.notes: This is a geotagged Bulgarian embassies and consulates. It includes the Ministry of Foreign Afairs [web page](http://mfa.bg) tag of the embassies, city&state, type, geo coords and full address. It was compiled for the preliminary voting registration project [Glasuvam.org](http://glasuvam.org/). It allows Bulgarians abroad to register their interest in voting outside of Bulgaria. This initiative and the partner sites will help them organize voting sections, register for voting, know their rights and find the closest voting booth.
package.title: All Bulgarian embassies and consulates

package.name: bulgarian-elections
package.author: Bulgarian Election Committee
package.notes: These is the data on the last 3 elections - EU parliament, BG parliament and the combined local/presidential elections in '09 to '11. All data is in CSV can be downloaded as a bulk from the Election Committee's [website](http://www.cikbg.org/).
package.title: Bulgarian Election results 2009-2011

package.name: bulgarian-court-docs
package.author: Bulgarian Courts
package.notes: This dataset contains 0.5 million decisions of Bulgarian courts since 2000 together with metadata. The information was scraped from the [judicial repository](http://legalacts.justice.bg/), which although public, has quite limited search capabilities. The metadata SQL database is added in this entry. The document dump is also available for download, but the link is provided per request due to its huge size. Please check the dataset's [site](http://opendata.yurukov.net/legalsystem/) for contacts.
package.title: Bulgarian court decisions
